description: Where every coefficient of the city's information, disaster and recovery models comes from (Phase 23). confidence: anchored = a study's value converts directly; derived = a study's value through a stated conversion assumption; assumed = no study gives a value (some support a direction). Sources were read from search abstracts; full texts were not reachable from the build environment. range is the span the sensitivity analysis sweeps.

time.note: Formal Spec 2.3: six-hour phases. A tick-clock city counts a tick as six hours for these conversions (assumption) and, having no time of day, half of each tick as night.

hazus_substation.title: Decision Automation for Electric Power Network Recovery — substation repair times synthesized from HAZUS-MH (about 1, 3, 7 and 30 days by damage state; earthquake functions)

utility_storms.title: Dobson et al., case studies of large storm outages — AEP restored about 50% of customers in 5 days, 10% waited over two weeks; FPL full restoration over two weeks

katrina_lam_2009.title: Lam et al. 2009, Business Return in New Orleans (PLOS ONE) — about 65% of businesses reopened by October 2007, 26 months after Katrina

katrina_lam_2012.title: Lam et al. 2012, Predictors of Business Return after Katrina (PLOS ONE) — flood depth is the strongest predictor; the first 6–9 months matter most

north_rhine_2024.title: Wiesehahn & Kaifie 2024, The impact of the 2021 flood on outpatient care in the North Rhine region (BMC Public Health) — 97% of affected practices lost power, over half had water supply damage, nearly 40% lost patient records; about 120 practices could not operate or only partly, over 40 were destroyed

oxford_roads_2025.title: Oxford study of the 2025 monsoon floods in Sindh and Punjab — road segments with at least 60% inundation are unusable

cape_town_2024.title: Imelda & Guo 2024, Crime in the dark: electricity rationing (Graduate Institute working paper) — 10 more outage hours a month raise crime by 2.6%, at night only

texas_outages.title: Lee et al., power outages and crime (draft) — no effect of the 2021 Texas rolling blackouts or short Austin outages on crime

walter_murphy_2018.title: Walter & Murphy 2018, How to unring the bell: a meta-analysis of correcting misinformation (Communication Monographs) — r = .35 overall, r = .14 for real-world misinformation

debunking_2023.title: Meta-analysis of debunking science-relevant misinformation (Nature Human Behaviour 2023) — on average not successful, d = 0.19, P = 0.131

mcguirk_burke.title: McGuirk & Burke, food prices and conflict in Africa (VoxEU) — one standard deviation higher consumer prices raise the probability of riots, demonstrations and violence against civilians by 14.4%

lagi_2011.title: Lagi, Bertrand & Bar-Yam 2011, The food crises and political instability in North Africa and the Middle East — food riots occur above an FAO food price index of 210

vosoughi_2018.title: Vosoughi, Roy & Aral 2018, The spread of true and false news online (Science) — falsehood spreads farther, faster, deeper and more broadly than truth

jiang_2021.title: Jiang, Gao & Zhuang 2021, Reciprocal spreading and debunking processes of online misinformation (Physica A 565) — SIR-type model fitted to the Hurricane Harvey immigration rumor; fitted values not obtained

repression_hicn_417.title: The Backlash Effect of State Coercion (HiCN working paper 417) — repression brings backlash in Uganda; findings across the literature contradict each other

repression_pvg_2020.title: The Political Backlash of Repressive Policing (Political Violence at a Glance, 2020) — arrests and beatings raise protest in Chile, rubber bullets deter; effects fade within weeks in the US

hazus_flood_manual.title: FEMA Hazus Flood Model Technical Manual 6.1 — depth–damage functions by occupancy (IND1–IND6); tables not read

coefficients.unit: pressure points per step while a district has less than a step's food
coefficients.finding: Food price rises raise the probability of riots and demonstrations (+14.4% per standard deviation), above a threshold.
coefficients.method: Direction and the threshold form (shortage is on or off) follow the studies; the size is not converted: the studies give a probability change, the model a pressure score.

coefficients.unit: pressure points per step without power, times the night share of the step
coefficients.finding: Outages raise crime at night only (Cape Town, +2.6% per 10 hours a month); the Texas blackouts show no effect.
coefficients.method: Timing follows the Cape Town study (night share of the step, see time.night_from / night_to); the size is not converted and may be zero (Texas).

coefficients.unit: pressure points per step in unrest (twice in riot)
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Chosen in Phase 22 so a district in unrest grows uneasy within a few steps.

coefficients.unit: share of a neighbour's higher pressure taken per step, times its communication
coefficients.finding: False news spreads farther and faster than true news; an SIR-type model was fitted to a Harvey rumor, but its fitted rates could not be read.
coefficients.method: Direction only; the rate is a Phase 22 choice.

coefficients.unit: share of a district's own pressure that fades per step
coefficients.finding: Rumor models carry forgetting rates; none with a value was read.
coefficients.method: A Phase 22 choice: pressure halves in about 7 steps (42 hours) without new causes.

coefficients.unit: public order points lost per step per 100 pressure
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: A Phase 22 choice, softened from 4 after the crisis city collapsed in a smoke run.

coefficients.unit: pressure at or above which a patrol backfires
coefficients.finding: Studies of repression and protest contradict each other.
coefficients.method: Mechanism kept; threshold is a Phase 22 choice.

coefficients.unit: pressure points a backfiring patrol adds
coefficients.finding: Arrests and beatings raised protest in Chile and Uganda; rubber bullets deterred; effects fade within weeks.
coefficients.method: Mechanism kept; size is a Phase 22 choice; the range includes no backlash.

coefficients.unit: share of a backfiring patrol's order gain lost
coefficients.finding: As backlash.
coefficients.method: A Phase 22 choice.

coefficients.unit: share of a district's pressure removed by one counter-message
coefficients.finding: Corrections move belief in misinformation by r = .35 on average, r = .14 for real-world misinformation; a 2023 meta-analysis finds debunking on average not successful (d = 0.19).
coefficients.method: The real-world effect size r = .14 is read as the share of pressure removed (an assumption: r is a correlation, not a share); the range runs to the overall r = .35. Replaces Phase 22's fixed 12 points.

coefficients.unit: pressure at which the city office starts counter-messaging
coefficients.finding: None: a policy threshold, not a property of the world.
coefficients.method: A Phase 22 choice for the baseline policy.

coefficients.unit: share of severity lost from a flooded district's food
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 22: food × (1 − severity).

coefficients.unit: share of severity lost from a flooded district's medical care
coefficients.finding: 2021 North Rhine flood: about 120 practices could not operate or only partly, over 40 were destroyed (about a third).
coefficients.method: At severity 0.6 medical care keeps 70% of itself, and the power cut (power_cut_at) halves what it can give (power.dark_medical): about a third left, near the study's picture of a third destroyed and the rest limited.

coefficients.unit: public order points lost at full severity
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 22: 10 × severity.

coefficients.unit: severity at or above which a flood cuts every road into its district
coefficients.finding: Road segments with at least 60% inundation are unusable (2025 Pakistan floods).
coefficients.method: Severity is read as the inundated share of the district's roads (an assumption). Phase 22 cut roads at any severity.

coefficients.unit: severity at or above which a flooded district has no power while the flood lasts
coefficients.finding: 97% of practices hit by the 2021 North Rhine flood lost power.
coefficients.method: 97% of affected sites is read as every flooded district (any severity). Phase 22 floods never cut power.

coefficients.unit: share of severity lost from a burning district's industry and its capacity
coefficients.finding: Hazus has occupancy depth–damage tables for floods; no fire table and no table values were read.
coefficients.method: Phase 22: industry × (1 − severity); Phase 23 burns the capacity behind it too, so it must be rebuilt (recovery.rebuild).

coefficients.unit: share of severity lost from a burning district's administration
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 22.

coefficients.unit: share of severity lost from a burning district's medical care
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 22.

coefficients.unit: public order points lost at full severity
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 22: 5 × severity.

coefficients.unit: industry a working district resumes per step, up to its capacity
coefficients.finding: None found: this is output resuming once power and order are back, not capacity being rebuilt.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: industry lost per step without power or in unrest or riot
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: industry capacity rebuilt per step after war or fire destroyed it
coefficients.finding: About 65% of New Orleans businesses had reopened 26 months after Katrina; flood depth was the strongest predictor.
coefficients.method: 0.65 over 26 months = 0.65 / (26 × 30.44 days × 4 steps a day) = 0.000206 a step at 6 hours a step. The range runs to ten times faster for damage lighter than Katrina's flooding.

coefficients.unit: administration regained per step while stable
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: administration lost per step in riot
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: administration one administer action adds
coefficients.finding: None found.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: steps of crew work to bring a failed substation back
coefficients.finding: Hazus-based restoration of a substation takes about 1 day for slight and 3 days for moderate damage (earthquake functions); after large storms about half of customers wait up to 5 days.
coefficients.method: Slight damage, 1 day = 24 hours / 6 hours a step = 4 steps; the range runs to moderate damage (3 days = 12 steps). Phase 14 used 3.

coefficients.unit: steps to reset a substation its protection tripped
coefficients.finding: None found: a trip is reset, not repaired.
coefficients.method: Phase 14.

coefficients.unit: public order points per step without power, times the night share of the step
coefficients.finding: Outages raise crime at night only (Cape Town, +2.6% per 10 hours a month); the Texas blackouts show no effect.
coefficients.method: Timing follows the Cape Town study (night share of the step); the size is Phase 14's and may be zero (Texas). On a tick clock, which has no time of day, a step counts half night.
